newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa crawls back but still down by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa crawls back but still down by close.

text.p: Cocoa futures crawled back in the afternoon from early lows but still ended lower on light spec liquidation, traders said.
Overall volume was just above 2,100 lots as most producers, manufacturers and traders stayed away from the market awaiting fresh fundamental news.
"Everybody seemed to be happy with their positions, there was no fresh news, the market was very quiet and prices drifted away," said one. "The specs were still long in London but not very much."
Benchmark September stood seven stg lower at 1,033 stg a tonne, the day's peak, after gapping 10 stg down and well below pre-opening expectations of two or three stg down.
It touched an intraday-low of 1,023 stg, the lowest level since July 4. After the immediate floor at 1,023-1,024, the contract faces a key support at 1,000.
Traders attributed the slide to light spec selling. Sterling's strength against the mark, the U.S. dollar and French francs also did not help the situation.
Technically, market points to a lower trend if the 1,023-1,024 support fails.
"Volume is not convincing...there could be further room on the downside," said one trader.
The upside potential is also limited, some said. Resistance is seen at 1,061, then the chart gap at between 1,087 and 1,108.
Fundamentally, there were no fresh developments to lure back larger players.
"They prefer to wait and be sure of the fundamental situation especially in Ivory Coast," they said
The strength of sterling against French francs could bring West African cocoa closer to the market.
Traders said although Ivorian of Ghanaian producers were well-hedged, origin selling could emerge if prices rise to around 1,080 level.
In spreads, Sept/Dec was trading at 24-25 stg while March/June traded at 29 stg.

Sterling/mark hit 3.0327, the highest since October 1990, on Monday, amid broad mark weakness. But it stood off peaks at 3.0244/55 marks in late European trading versus 2.9985/95 late Friday in Europe.
Sterling's jump also came at the back of persistent expectations of higher UK interest rates.
